conviction_note: The print lands on the Q4 guide against a Q4 consensus near $410-427M. Peers beat this quarter (COHR, FN, LITE) and Amazon, the anchor customer, raised its 2027 capex language, but the 1.6T DSP/TIA shortage is real and the tape sold COHR's beat-and-raise by 14% on Nov 5. So the findings roughly offset (impact_sum -0.7). p_up is 49 on an abs_move of 19, the 18.4% straddle nudged up for 117% realised vol and Nov 6 payrolls inside the window. The two numbers agree in sign and are both near zero. The size sits in abs_move, not in direction.

findings.finding: Every optics peer that has reported this cycle beat. Coherent's Q1 FY27 revenue was $2.37B against $2.31B consensus, with a Q2 guide of $2.55-2.75B above estimates (Nov 4). Fabrinet's Q1 FY27 revenue was $1.474B against its own $1.375-1.425B guide. Lumentum printed $1.26B inside its $1.225-1.275B guide. That supports AAOI landing at or above its $272.5M guide midpoint against the $269M consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue of $191.9M, inside the $180-198M guide, traded +9.19%. Q1 2026 missed ($151.1M, EPS -$0.07 vs -$0.05 expected) and traded -5.46%. In this tape Coherent's beat-and-raise opened +5% and closed down 14% on Nov 5.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $269M sits below the guide midpoint and EPS at $0.14 near the low end, so the street is shading the quarter down despite the peers. If the peer beats were priced, AAOI's revenue consensus would sit at or above the midpoint rather than 1% below it. The capacity-bound model means revenue equals output, and peers show output was not demand-limited.
findings.independence: Fabrinet: https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/fabrinet-steigert-gewinnsprung-und-hebt-q1-prognose-umsatz-und-eps-liegen-klar-uber-erwartungen. Lumentum: https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2027-Financial-Results/default.aspx. These are separate documents from the Coherent source. All are proxies, not AAOI's own number.

findings.finding: Amazon is AAOI's anchor hyperscale customer (the $200M+ 1.6T order went to a long-time hyperscale partner). On Oct 29 Amazon reiterated ~$220B of 2026 capex, said 2027 would be 'meaningfully more', and reported AWS +39% with a $578B backlog. All of this came after AAOI last spoke on Aug 6, and it supports a firm Q4/2027 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Forward-volume prints moved this stock most: Feb 2026 +56.88% on the Q4 beat and Q1 outlook, Aug 2026 +9.19% on the fivefold 800G guide. The May 2026 Q2 guide miss traded -5.46%.
findings.why_not_priced: AAOI fell about 45% after Amazon's call, so the market is discounting hyperscaler demand transmission to AAOI or AAOI's ability to capture it. If priced, AAOI would have tracked the capex raise. The customer-to-AAOI link is not confirmed until AAOI guides.
findings.independence: Constellation Research on the same Amazon print: https://www.constellationr.com/insights/news/aws-q3-revenue-growth-surges-39-capex-stings-amazons-cash-flow. Same underlying event. Customer identity is inferred from the March order release: https://convergedigest.com/aoi-lands-200m-hyperscaler-order-for-transceivers/. Proxy.

findings.finding: On Oct 30 AAOI replaced its $35M-unused BOKF facility with a $200M East West Bank-led facility: $170M term loan for buying or refinancing equipment, a $30M revolver, and a $50M accordion, at SOFR+2.50-3.25%, maturing 2030 (8-K filed Nov 4). That is bank-underwritten capacity funding on top of the $588M net ATM completed Oct 5.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Equity financing has been sold: the stock fell about 14% when the $600M ATM was disclosed in Aug 2026 and 13.6% on Oct 8 after the completion release. No prior debt facility reaction found.
findings.why_not_priced: A quiet 8-K filed the day before the print with no press release. Debt funding equipment lowers the odds of a fourth ATM at $47, against three this year, each filed within about two weeks of a print. If priced, the dilution overhang would show less in the discount to the $105 ATM price.
findings.independence: Use of proceeds matches the capacity ramp stated in the Q2 release (650k units/month 800G+1.6T by year-end): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1158114/000168316826006055/aaoi_ex9901.htm. The ATM completion and its use of proceeds for equipment: https://www.webull.com/news/15695286338012160.

findings.finding: A Nomura expert call (Sept 23) put the 2026 shortfall of 1.6T transceiver DSPs at 3-4M units, widening to 20M+ in 2027 (TSMC 3nm-bound). AAOI itself named DSPs and TIAs as its main constraint. That puts at risk the Q4 conversion of the $200M+ 1.6T order (mostly Q4) and a Q4 guide that has to meet $410-427M consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 print, with a Q2 guide below expectations, traded -5.46%. Intra-quarter CPO delay reports in June 2026 cost 5-8% on single days (itiger stock-track items).
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 consensus of $410M+ needs roughly +50-55% sequential growth. If the street had priced a component-bound Q4, estimates would sit closer to Q3 plus capacity added, not at a figure that assumes the DSPs arrive. Coherent says it is not assembly-constrained, so the shortage hits non-vertically-integrated DSP buyers like AAOI more.
findings.independence: AAOI's own Aug 6 call commentary on two components in short supply, via Trefis: https://www.trefis.com/articles/618154/one-reason-to-buy-applied-optoelectronics-stock-now/2026-10-09. Yole on 200G/lane supply chokepoints: https://www.yolegroup.com/strategy-insights/opinion-optical-transceivers-at-the-chokepoint-of-ai-growth-and-supply-chain-constraints/. Shortened slightly for ~15% short interest.

findings.finding: The bar has been cut hard. Q3 EPS consensus fell from $0.28 to $0.14 over 90 days with six straight cuts, and the next-quarter revenue estimate is down 3.65% over 3 months. EPS now sits near the low end of the $0.11-0.26 guide, with a $0.12 whisper.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AAOI beat Zacks EPS 3 of the last 4 quarters (average surprise 40%). Reactions ranged from -5.46% to +56.88%, so EPS beats alone have not reliably paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely in the wire. The residual unpriced part: an EPS bar at the bottom of the guide makes an in-guide print read as a beat. ATM dilution (about 5.7M more shares than the guide's 92.8M base) explains part of the cut.
findings.independence: EarningsWhispers $0.14 consensus / $0.12 whisper: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/AAOI/22220. Same bar from a different aggregator.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out: -40% in 5 sessions and -55% in 20, $47.5 against the $105.36 ATM average price, about 10x a $4.60 2027 EPS estimate, and roughly 15% of float short. A guide that holds the capacity ramp has a squeeze-and-rerate path. The drawdown is explained by a sector/macro selloff, not by anything company-specific.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026: +56.88% into a crowded short ('shorts pressured', rallies.ai). Aug 2026: +9.19%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced by definition: the straddle is 18.4%. The asymmetric part is that the stock already sits 55% below where it was before any company news, so a neutral guide removes a fear the price holds.
findings.independence: Short interest 13.87M shares, 2.0 days to cover (sweep row, massive.com). Benzinga 16.9% of float: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AAOI/sentiment. Shares the 247wallst document with the bar finding.

findings.finding: The Nov 4-5 tape sells beats in this group. On Nov 5 AAOI fell ~20% to $47.42, Coherent fell 14% after a beat-and-raise (it had opened +5%), and Lumentum fell 13% and Fabrinet 13%. The trigger was a Democratic sweep and data-center regulation fears, plus a Qualcomm memory-cost warning. Nov 6 payrolls also fall inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Coherent's same-week beat-and-raise closed down 14%. Fabrinet's Aug 2026 beat gapped down about 14%. Sector reaction function: beats sold.
findings.why_not_priced: This is not mispricing. It is the reaction function: a good AAOI print may still be sold if the macro de-risking continues on Nov 6. If it were fully priced, Coherent's beat would have held its opening gain.
findings.independence: Pre-election risk framing, including Hartnett's 10%-drop scenario on a Democratic sweep: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-10-22/investors-see-risk-us-midterms-ai-trade-data-center-backlash-builds. Macro proxy.

findings.finding: The Q3 guide already carries a $20-25M drop in 100G sales because a customer cannot source memory-constrained switches. On Nov 5 Qualcomm warned of rising memory costs and Micron reportedly paused a Taiwan plant, so the memory shortage may persist into Q4 and extend the 100G headwind into the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 100G headwind was disclosed with the Q2 print, which still traded +9.19%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 piece is inside the guide and priced. Only the Q4 extension is unpriced. It is a 100G segment item now small against the 800G ramp (fivefold sequential) and CATV ($100-110M guide), so it is sized net of the rest of the company.
findings.independence: Qualcomm and Micron memory items per https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/05/applied-optoelectronics-sinks-16-coherent-tumbles-14-despite-strong-outlook-lumentum-plunges-13-as-ai-optical-stocks-slide/. Proxy.

baseline_tension: There is no skew reading (null), and put/call OI is 0.78. The -55% run-up says the market already holds a lot of fear. What I found is mixed: peers beat and the anchor customer is accelerating, against a DSP-bound Q4 and a tape that sells beats. It neither confirms nor contradicts the run-up, which is why p_up sits at 49 and the size sits in abs_move.
